title: A von-Mangoldt prime-power dissipative law and its missing xi intertwiner
question: Can strict global dissipation be derived directly from arithmetic rather than postulated on the zero support?

verdict.conclusion: Normalizing Lambda(n)n^(-2-2eta) gives a genuine prime-power exponential family.  Its Fisher-natural gradient of relative entropy to the eta=0 prime ledger is exactly d eta/dt=-eta, with strict dissipation and golden time log(phi).  A finite positive reflection-symmetric mixture equals the central prime ledger only when all displacements vanish.  However, the actual explicit formula is signed and oscillatory through cos(gamma log x); it does not identify the xi divisor with that positive mixture.  Squaring returns the previously unresolved prime-pair energy theorem.  The arithmetic law is proved, but its same-xi intertwiner is not, so RH remains open.

finiteComputation.scope: the identities are analytic for the infinite convergent family; the finite rows are deterministic numerical checks on the truncated family

positiveMixtureRigidity.statement: for a finite positive mixture of reflected states p_eta and p_-eta, equality with p_0 at every prime power forces every eta=0
positiveMixtureRigidity.tailProof: if eta_max>0, the p_-eta_max/p_0 ratio grows like n^(2eta_max) along prime powers and cannot equal a constant central tail with positive coefficients
positiveMixtureRigidity.conditionalRhClosure: if the actual completed zero ledger were proved to induce such a positive mixture equal to p_0, rigidity would force RH
